summary: Jefferson County, OR three-story enclosed tower (1963) on Stephenson Mountain; Forest Service staffed; destroyed by the Box Springs Fire on July 20, 2026.

facts.design: Enclosed three-story wooden tower (NHLR: ODF modified L-4; Oregon Lookouts: Amort Special)
facts.status_note: Destroyed by the Box Springs Fire on July 20, 2026, per ODF statement and the Register; no source describes what remains on the site

staffing.status: Staffed by the Forest Service until the July 2026 fire; occupant evacuated

access.note: Cheryl Hill and firelookout.com say private land with no public access; NHLR says ODF land transferred to the Ochoco National Forest in the late 1980s. Sources disagree.

visit.trail_note: Tower destroyed in 2026; no source describes a public route to the site

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry; Ochoco National Forest (U.S. Forest Service) from the late 1980s

events.note: First lookout on the site, a tree platform, per NHLR and Central Oregon Daily; firelookout.com dates a crow's nest to the mid-1920s
Tree platform replaced by a 60-foot wooden tower with a ground house
Current three-story enclosed tower; firelookout.com gives 1962 to 1963 and Oregon Lookouts dates the work from 1962
Manned full time for the first time in four years, with joint BLM, Ochoco National Forest and state funding
Box Springs Fire reached the site at about 4 a.m. on July 20
Structure destroyed; communication towers and a radio repeater at the site were lost or affected

resolved_conflicts.explanation: ODF and the Register name the Box Springs Fire; Cheryl Hill names the Rowe Creek Complex, a wider group of fires. The story uses the ODF name and notes the other.
The Register and Central Oregon Daily give 1963; firelookout.com and Oregon Lookouts date the work to 1962 and 1963. The story gives 1963 as the completion year and notes the 1962 start.

notes_for_editor: Loss in July 2026 is well sourced (ODF statement quoted by Central Oregon Daily and the Register, plus two news and lookout sites). Unresolved: the first-lookout date (1931 tree platform vs mid-1920s crow's nest), the design name (ODF modified L-4 vs Amort Special), and whether the site is private land or ODF land later transferred to the Ochoco National Forest. Elevation differs (Register 5,788 ft / 1,764 m; firelookout.com 5956 ft), so elevation_m was not added to facts. Statesman Journal returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The brief's record matches the sources; no corrections. Used 1 WebSearch and 6 page reads.
